learning: If the S-bend and slalom losses clear, over-correction at bend onset was the cause. If they persist with kp reduced, the cause is more likely the start pose or the line-loss handling, and the next test should report where on the course the loss begins.
notes: Geometry held at the iteration 5 and 7 values. Controller moves to kp 2.2, kd 0.3, ki 0, base_speed 1.1 to test whether less proportional gain and more damping clear the S-bend and slalom line losses that persisted through iterations 5 and 7.
rationale: Iteration 7 (kp 2.8, kd 0.25, base_speed 1.1) on the iteration 5 geometry scored 53.68. Oval line loss stayed at 0. S-bend and slalom each still logged 1 loss, with max_error about 0.060 to 0.064 m. Lowering base_speed (iter 5) and raising kp with more kd (iter 7) did not clear those losses, and max_error did not move. Mass (0.7 to 0.6 kg) and span (+/-0.05 m) are already settled by iterations 3 to 5, so the remaining levers are controller-side. Geometry is held exactly as in iteration 7 per the Builder's intent and the Integrator's decision rules. This package changes the controller only. kp goes from 2.8 to 2.2 to reduce the overshoot that a strong correction at bend onset may cause. kd goes from 0.25 to 0.30 to damp that overshoot. ki is set to 0 because the integral has not shown a benefit and adds windup on curves. base_speed stays at 1.1 so that the speed effect is not confounded. line_loss stays at last_direction so the controller-side change is the only variable. Expected result: if the S-bend and slalom losses are caused by overshoot from over-correction, they fall to 0 and progress rises. If the losses stay at 1, the cause is the start pose or the line-loss handling, and the next step is to report the course position where the loss begins rather than to edit geometry. This is an untested guess; the score is expected near 53 to 56.
